elements.element: Customer pays no liquidated damages or penalties.
elements.evidence: Revised 23.2 now reads "the defaulting Party shall not be liable for any liquidated damages or penalty in respect of the reclaimed capacity" and "Amounts already paid by the defaulting Party under this Agreement shall not be forfeited." The two Customer-payable penalty mechanics in the cited text (denial of any payment or credit for capacity taken on default, and forfeiture of all amounts already paid) are gone, and no other Customer-payable liquidated amount, minimum termination fee, or penalty formula survives in the rendered clause. What remains against Customer is only reclamation of capacity for genuine payment default and liability for accrued unpaid accounts incurred before reclamation — actual accrued debt, not a liquidated sum.

elements.element: Any Customer-payable liquidated amount is only an early-termination fee.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: after the edit there is no Customer-payable liquidated amount of any kind in 23.1–23.2, so the restriction is satisfied vacuously by the stronger preferred outcome.

elements.element: The early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: no early-termination fee or minimum-fee-on-exit mechanic is imposed on Customer in the rendered language, so there is no amount requiring a three-month cap.

elements.element: The early-termination fee is the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: Customer owes no liquidated amount at all under the revised 23.2 (only accrued unpaid accounts), so the "sole amount" constraint is met vacuously.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: the breach-triggered forfeiture of all amounts paid and the denial of any payment or credit for reclaimed capacity — the only Customer-payable penalty mechanics in the cited text — are both removed, and the replacement language is an unconditional statement that Customer bears no liquidated damages or penalty. No retained formula, instalment, or contingent payment mechanic runs against Customer.

Minimal: exactly two surgical replacements inside 23.2, both aimed at penalty mechanics within the LD checklist. Favourable and neutral existing language survives untouched — the extenuating-circumstances duty, the notice/cure sequence in 23.1, the Management Committee's disposition power, termination of rights on full reclamation, and continuing liability for unpaid accounts incurred before reclamation. No survival tail, damages carve-out, procedure, or boilerplate was added, and no unrelated rule (exit economics under 18.1, default interest under 7.8) was touched.

Intent preserved: reclamation remains available for real payment default, accrued-debt liability is expressly retained, the Schedules-revision and reallocation mechanics are intact, and no cross-reference or defined term is left dangling.

Non-blocking drafting notes for the negotiator (do not change the completeness assessment): (i) the inserted no-LD sentence is scoped "in respect of the reclaimed capacity"; that is coextensive with the only trigger in this clause, but if Vendor proposes penalty language elsewhere, insist on an unscoped formulation; (ii) "shall not be forfeited" bars retention as a penalty but does not itself state a repayment mechanic — if Vendor pushes back, consider "shall be refunded to the extent they relate to capacity reclaimed" rather than accepting reinstatement of the forfeiture; (iii) the retained sentence "All rights of a defaulting Party under this Agreement shall terminate as of the time all its capacity ... is reclaimed" is prospective and is followed by the specific non-forfeiture sentence, so it does not contradict the fix, but be alert to Vendor arguing otherwise.
